A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging impairs pDCs in the production of type I interferon (IFN) in response to viral infection.
aging impairs IFN regulatory factor 7 up-regulation in pDCs during TLR9-activation, and this alteration leads to impaired IFN- α production and viral clearance with aging.
aging impairs pDCs in their ability to produce type I IFNs, and this defect contributes to increased susceptibility of older individuals to viral infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging impairs the ability of plasmacytoid DCs to produce IFN-β in response to viral infection, which in turn leads to increased susceptibility to viral infections in older people.
aging impairs the function of pDCs, the innate immune sensors that are responsible for the production of IFN-α during viral infection.
aging impairs the function of a subset of innate immune cells that are key to the host defense against viral infections.
